title: release-redactions
description: monitor/release-redactions.json — names that must not appear in the PUBLIC REPOSITORY. Consumed by bin/test/release-names.test.mjs, which validates against THIS schema rather than re-implementing it, so there is one statement of the shape and not two. Distinct from schema/publish-redactions.schema.json: that governs the docsite publish boundary over a client-only population, this governs the repository release over a wider one that includes the operator's own products. Merging them would redact commitwork's own tool names from its own public documentation.

note.description: Why this file exists and how it differs from publish-redactions. Required: a redaction set with no rationale is one nobody can audit, and this one's whole subtlety is that it is NOT the other one.

names.description: One entry per identity to remove. Order is not significant; the consumer sorts longest-first so a longer name is consumed before a shorter one it contains.

name.description: The source identity. Whitespace is refused: a key containing it would never match a rendered identifier, so it would silently redact nothing.

replacement.description: Provisional until the operator finalises it. Non-empty: an empty replacement deletes the surrounding sentence's subject and leaves prose reading as though nothing was removed.

scope.description: `all` — every occurrence goes, including paths and filenames. `prose` — occurrences go EXCEPT those matching `exempt`, which are external contracts this repo does not own and cannot rename without breaking an integration.

exempt.description: Substrings marking an occurrence as an external contract that stays. Only meaningful with scope `prose`. Every entry must be VERIFIED present in the tree, not assumed — an exemption for a form that does not exist silently widens the carve-out.

replacementAlternatives.description: Further acceptable replacements where ONE name does not fit every site, because the identity plays more than one role. The reviewer picks per occurrence. Only meaningful alongside `reviewPerSite`: a set of alternatives with no per-site review is an invitation to pick the first one everywhere and call it done.

reviewPerSite.description: True when the test for redaction is a JUDGEMENT no substring rule makes — typically because the name is also an ordinary word in this repo's subject matter. The consumer still enumerates every occurrence, but the count is a REVIEW list rather than a replace list, and it must not be mass-substituted.

ruling.description: The operator's words and the measurement behind them, where an entry needed a decision rather than a rule. Kept verbatim so a later reader can see what was decided rather than inferring it from the outcome.

undetermined.description: Substrings whose status is genuinely unsettled — not known-exempt, not known-in-scope. The consumer reports these in their own bucket, outside pass and fail, rather than resolving them by guess. Absence of a ruling is its own state and is displayed as such.

why.description: The ruling and its evidence. Required: an identity in a redaction set with no stated reason cannot be re-litigated by a later reader, who will not know whether it was measured or assumed.

outOfScope.description: Names deliberately NOT redacted, with the reason. Recorded so a deliberate asymmetry does not read as an oversight to the next reader — the one failure mode a redaction set cannot self-diagnose.
